clue.text: Boat outside harbour provides staff in Equity

indicators.note: the boat sits on the outside, wrapping round the word for a harbour

blocks.note: SS, steamship, the prefix on a ship's name
a port is a harbour
to man something is to staff it
in and hip both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A boat moored outside a harbour supplies workers who belong to Equity, the actors' union.
explanation.walkthrough: Equity looks like the actors' union, staffing a boat; here it is fairness. In, meaning fashionable, is a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is fairness and even-handedness, and sportsmanship is fair play towards opponents, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Items sold at school fetes made by PTA?

blocks.note: the P of the abbreviation, taken as written
the TA that follows: the Territorial Army, Britain's army reserve

explanation.surface: Jams and cakes on a stall at a school fair, made by the parent-teacher association.
explanation.walkthrough: PTA reads as the parent-teacher association that runs school fetes, but it splits into P and TA. The Territorial Army is the British Army's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Preserves are home-made jams, marmalades and pickles, staple goods on a school fair stall.

clue.text: Clever to cover head when this?

definitions.text: Clever to cover head when this?

indicators.note: covering the head hides the first letter, so the word is read without its opening

blocks.note: brainy means clever

explanation.surface: A bit of weather advice: it is sensible to wear a hat when it is wet outside.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAINY loses its head B to give RAINY; read as a whole, the clue says a clever person covers their head in this weather.
explanation.definitionFit: On a rainy day a sensible person wears a hood or hat, so the whole clue describes the weather it names.

clue.text: It's normal to stop on a road

blocks.note: to stand is to stop still
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A driver's grumble that halting on a road is just ordinary practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard as an adjective means usual or ordinary, the same as normal.

clue.text: Evoke a river — one in the northeast

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, in the north-east of England

explanation.surface: A writer trying to conjure the mood of a northern river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back to river: the Ouse is a river flowing through York.
explanation.definitionFit: To arouse a feeling is to call it up or stir it, which is what evoke means.

clue.text: Accordingly a religious big-wig and artist get together for programme

blocks.note: so means accordingly, therefore
taken as written
the Pope is the head of the Catholic Church
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A churchman and a painter team up to make a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial television or radio drama, a kind of programme.

clue.text: One heading for snow protected by mountain is a famous Norwegian

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept
something protected by another is surrounded and shielded by it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
the first letter of snow

explanation.surface: A skier from Norway heads for the snowy peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside BEN, and I comes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen, author of A Doll's House and Peer Gynt, is Norway's most celebrated playwright.

clue.text: Dressing required after hairdresser cut Rod on cheek

indicators.note: a word that is cut is trimmed, here losing its final letter

blocks.note: a barber is a men's hairdresser
a cue is the rod used in snooker and billiards
sauce is impudence, cheek

explanation.surface: After a nasty slip by the hairdresser, Rod needs a bandage on his cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressing suggests a bandage for a cut, and Rod looks like a man's name; it is a snooker cue, and the dressing is a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing can be any sauce poured over food, and barbecue sauce is a tangy condiment for grilled meat.

clue.text: Private Eye, say, connects famous people

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: personal means private
the letter I is pronounced like eye
ties means connects

explanation.surface: The satirical magazine Private Eye links celebrities, as its gossip pages do.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine famous for gossip about public figures, which makes the split between Private and Eye hard to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Personalities are celebrities, people well known to the public.

clue.text: Not oddly, David Cameron prepared a drink

indicators.note: taking the letters that are not in odd positions leaves the even ones
something prepared has been made up from its ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of David, the ones in even positions
taken as written

explanation.surface: The former Prime Minister David Cameron, behaving normally, makes someone a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Not oddly looks like a comment on Cameron's behaviour; it picks the even letters of David.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is a coffee made by adding hot water to espresso, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Drink is taken in part of church

indicators.note: something taken in is absorbed inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: ale is a drink, beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sipping a drink in a side area of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The aisle is the passage between the pews or alongside the nave, part of a church's layout.

clue.text: Strong worker's extremely friendly

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a worker bee; worker is a stock crossword clue for bee or ant
the first and last letters of friendly

explanation.surface: A sturdy labourer who is very warm and sociable.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefy means brawny and muscular, physically strong.

clue.text: Some French bombs outside old city on the plains

indicators.note: the bombs lie outside, around the single letter for old

blocks.note: des is French for some
mines are explosive devices, bombs
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: French explosives planted outside an ancient city on the plains.
explanation.walkthrough: Des is the French partitive article meaning some, as in des pommes.
explanation.definitionFit: Des Moines is the capital of Iowa, a state of the American Great Plains region.

clue.text: Place heater in cold crack

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
an oven heats food
to have a crack at something is to have a try

explanation.surface: An instruction to fit a heater into a draughty crack in a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Place looks like a verb, an instruction, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands, so it is a place.

clue.text: Too much booze and dancing here and it might dawn on you!

definitions.text: Too much booze and dancing here and it might dawn on you!

blocks.clueFragment: Too much booze and dancing here
blocks.note: surface reading: a warning about a heavy night out

blocks.clueFragment: and it might dawn on you!
blocks.note: setter's reading: dance here late enough and the sun comes up while you are still inside, a venue open through the dark hours

explanation.walkthrough: Dawn on you sounds like a sudden realisation; literally it means the night ends and day breaks while you are still there.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a venue for drinking and dancing that stays open late into the small hours.

clue.text: Admiral in the hold

blocks.note: first meaning: Horatio ..., victor of Trafalgar
second meaning: a wrestling hold applied from behind the opponent's arms and neck

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an admiral down in a ship's hold, but hold is a wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiral Lord Nelson is Britain's most famous naval commander, and a nelson is also a named wrestling grip.

clue.text: Butcher starting to sell best medicine?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of sell
from the proverb that laughter is the best medicine

explanation.surface: A butcher getting started on selling the finest cuts, or the best remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher is a verb here, not the shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people or animals is to kill them brutally, to slaughter them.

clue.text: Distressing detail about poor nag

indicators.note: something in poor shape is in disarray, so its letters are jumbled
about means around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a point is a detail or particular
the letters of nag rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad piece of news about an old horse in bad shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Poor reads as pity for the horse, but it is the signal to rearrange the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignant describes something that evokes a keen sense of sadness, so it is distressing.

clue.text: Flag officer

blocks.note: first meaning: a flag flown on a ship to show nationality
second meaning: a junior commissioned officer in the US Navy

explanation.walkthrough: Flag officer is a real naval rank for an admiral, which hides the two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is both a naval flag and the lowest commissioned rank in the US Navy.

clue.text: It's a pleasure to see absence of rubbish at the shops — no hint of muck

indicators.note: no hint of a word means its first letter is taken away

blocks.note: no expresses absence
tat is cheap rubbish
a mall is a shopping centre
the opening letter of muck, which is taken away

explanation.surface: A shopper relieved to find a tidy shopping centre with no litter or grime.
explanation.walkthrough: The M of MALL is dropped to leave ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Not at all is the polite reply to thanks, meaning the same as it's a pleasure or you're welcome.

clue.text: Almost come into contact with an arboreal dweller

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to touch is to come into contact with
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nearly getting close to a creature living in the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a big-billed tropical bird that lives in forest trees, so it dwells in trees.

clue.text: Jazz leader — one requesting "Fly me to the moon"?

definitions.text: one requesting "Fly me to the moon"?

blocks.note: first meaning: Louis ..., the trumpeter and bandleader

blocks.clueFragment: one requesting "Fly me to the moon"?
blocks.note: second meaning: Neil ..., the first man to walk on the moon

explanation.walkthrough: Fly Me to the Moon is a jazz standard, which ties it to the first definition; the question mark flags that it is really a wish to be flown to the moon, as the astronaut was.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong led jazz bands, and astronaut Neil Armstrong flew to the moon on Apollo 11 in 1969.

clue.text: Note copied about a city

indicators.note: about means around, so the repeated note wraps the other piece

blocks.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale, written twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician copying out a note about a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Copied means the note appears twice, and A sits between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a major city in Florida in the United States.

clue.text: Those at the front of May's injured government have finally bought power

indicators.note: the letters at the front of the next several words are the ones kept
finally picks out the last letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the first letters of May's, injured, government and have
the last letter of bought

explanation.surface: A comment on Theresa May's damaged government buying its way to power.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister 2016-19, and her weakened government relied on a deal with the DUP that critics said was bought.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is strength or force, and so is power.

clue.text: Some feel embarrassed about fracas

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used
about means turned around, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Feeling ashamed about a brawl one was involved in.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused, noisy fight, a fracas or scuffle.

clue.text: Fresh chlorine put round something used at the pool

indicators.note: one element is put round the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine
raw means fresh, uncooked or new

explanation.surface: New chlorine added to the water at the swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: Chlorine looks like part of the pool scene, but only its symbol is used, wrapped round RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The crawl is the front swimming stroke, used by swimmers in a pool.

clue.text: Hot claret poured around pudding

indicators.note: liquid poured around is splashed everywhere, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Mulled red wine poured over a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a pudding of fruit or cream set in a mould lined with bread, sponge or biscuits.

clue.text: Grabbing toy he trashed Lemaître's idea

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A child snatches a toy and wrecks the physicist's model.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Lemaître, a Belgian priest and physicist, first proposed that the universe expanded from a primeval atom, the origin of the Big Bang theory.
